status: Code-only slice applying the three owner rulings on the A28 ClamAV findings. Not lab-observed: no clamd was run, no container was built and no stack was started (another executor holds the machine's lab and Docker). Every claim below is read out of the code and pinned by a test that was verified RED before the change; the behaviour against a REAL clamd is INT-04's already-passing A28 lane, which this slice does not re-run.
scope: Rulings on A28 findings 1 (a malware rejection is invisible to the creator), 2 (fail-open has no audit trail) and the CLAMAV_ADDR-unset default (silently unscanned), plus the ingestion-scope gap A28 recorded as unprobed: thumbnails, avatars, channel banners and account-import archives.
search_revision: vidra-search NOT touched and NOT run

pull_requests.ordering: No OpenAPI schema changed (the two new error codes are prose in the ErrorResponse envelope, not an enum), so there is no contract-ci ordering and no client regeneration. core#201 is merged. The meta templates are no longer version-gated: they are safe on the currently pinned v0.6.2 (which reads MALWARE_SCAN_ENABLED=false from its own compose default and simply does not scan; clamd runs idle) and turn scanning on by themselves once the pin advances to a release carrying #201.

template_posture.production_and_staging: CLAMAV_ADDR=clamav:3310 ACTIVE, MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=fail-closed ACTIVE, `scan` added to VIDRA_COMPOSE_PROFILES, and `# MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled` documented as the commented opt-out with its costs (boot WARN, one system.malware_scan.disabled audit row per boot, every user-supplied file stored unscanned, and the boot refusal if it is combined with a set CLAMAV_ADDR).
template_posture.dev_templates: local/dev-remote/qa keep MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled ACTIVE, deliberately and with the reason in the file: the Makefile dev targets hardcode `--profile core --profile frontend` and never start the bundled clamd, so an active CLAMAV_ADDR would make fail-closed refuse every upload on `make dev`. A dev box that ingests unscanned is precisely what the opt-out exists for, and it now says so in a WARN and an audit row.
template_posture.corrected_from: an earlier draft of this branch shipped MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled ACTIVE in production and staging too, which would have opted every fresh install out of the ruled posture.
template_posture.ram: clamd holds ~1.5-2 GiB resident for its signature database; the production template states this beside the address, because a 2 GB droplet is not enough with scanning on.

deploy_guard.finding: `vidra setup --scan=false` drops `scan` from VIDRA_COMPOSE_PROFILES and LEAVES CLAMAV_ADDR untouched. Verified by building the engine from core main (492da35) and running it with --scan=false and --scan=true against the edited template. Hand-editing either line produces the same pair.
deploy_guard.consequence: an instance that boots healthy, passes its health probes, and then refuses every upload, URL import, poster, avatar, banner, caption track, playlist cover, instance-branding image and DM attachment — fail-closed cannot reach a container nothing started, and no log line mentions a profile.
deploy_guard.fix: deploy/deploy.sh require_scanner_profile(), a 0/6 pre-flight beside the existing checks. It ADDS a check and does not touch the sacred dump -> pull -> migrate -> up -> probe ordering. It fires only for the BUNDLED `clamav` service name: an external clamd is the operator's own host, which this project neither starts nor can verify. The refusal names all three remedies (add the profile, point at an external clamd, or take the documented opt-out) and quotes the MALWARE_SCAN_MODE actually in force.
deploy_guard.tests: tests/scanner_profile_test.py — 6 tests lifting the function out of the real script (the tests/rollback_floor_test.py idiom), verified RED by neutering the guard.
deploy_guard.still_open_upstream: core's setup engine remains able to emit the incoherent pair; the deploy guard catches it at deploy time rather than at generation time. A follow-up in vidra-core could make --scan=false clear CLAMAV_ADDR (or set the opt-out) so the engine never writes a configuration it would refuse to run.
